messages:
alex: Quick docs PR ask: need a compact example for 'tenant surge' handling — show autoscale policy + isolation labels + fallback model routing. Trying to keep it one small code block + short text. Anyone can draft?

jamie: I can take a first pass. Do we want k8s-style YAML or Terraform snippet? +1 for YAML example for quickstart

cheng: YAML sounds good. include annotations for 'isolation: soft' vs 'isolation: strict' and note SLA impact. Also show rollback to lower-capacity model.

alex: Yes — show two policies: aggressive scale (low cooldown) for burst, and conservative (longer cooldown) for steady usage. And a note: billing impact and token cost.

jamie: Draft below. LMK edits.```yaml
# autoscale policy (burst)
name: tenant-burst
min_replicas: 1
max_replicas: 20
cpu_threshold_pct: 65
cooldown_seconds: 30
annotations:
  isolation: strict
  tenant_quota_label: "premium"
# fallback: route to gptq-quantized when capacity constrained
routing:
  fallback_model: "gptq-1.3b-quant"
```

lina: Nice. Can we also add quick text: when to use 'strict' vs 'soft' and how SLA changes? e.g., strict=>dedicated pool, higher cost, higher SLO. Soft=>shared pool, possible preemption.

cheng: Also add a short troubleshooting tip: if tenants hit eviction loops, check 'reserved_pool' assignment and scalepolicy cooldown.

docs-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4321 — added jamie's snippet + rationale. reviewers: @alex @cheng

alex: :thumbsup: I'll review this afternoon. Add a one-line example of CLI to assign tenant label: `rwctl tenant set-label --tenant-id t-123 --label isolation=strict`

jamie: Added CLI line in the PR. small nit: change cpu_threshold to 70 to match runtime defaults. pushing update.

cheng: LGTM after threshold change. Can we add a short 'cost note' line: estimated $0.12/hr per replica on p4d equivalent? keep it approximate.

alex: Good. After merges, I'll add to the provisioning checklist. thanks team.
